acceptanceCriteria: The preview writes no file under .corvint and is byte-identical to what a real index run stores for that file.
Output is an error envelope on an unparsed or untracked file, not plain text.
Documented in the owning spec as a read command.
body: Owner requested this on 2026-09-23 after reviewing Tencent/WeKnora (MIT) as prior art; this ticket records an idea, not delivery or promotion. Original Go work only; no source import. WeKnora is an LLM-at-ingest, database-backed RAG platform, so only the mechanism is borrowed and it must stay deterministic, local and read-only under AGENTS.md invariants 4 and 7. Before implementation is called complete, update the owning indexed spec with stable requirements, non-goals, failure modes, acceptance evidence and rollback, and finish normal CEM/OCM, independent review and mandatory gates. Prior art: website-docs/03-features/04-chunking.md of https://github.com/Tencent/WeKnora. `POST /api/v1/chunker/preview` shows how a document would be segmented under given parameters without any database write, and the docs note that a changed chunking config otherwise requires a re-parse to observe. Current state: the only way to see how Corvint turns a file into rows, declarations and (once V1-0096 and the breadcrumb ticket land) match text is to rebuild the index and query it. Idea: a read command, for example `corvint index --preview PATH`, that prints the rows, spans and match text the indexer would produce for one file at the current revision and writes nothing, honouring invariant 4. Owning spec: the index lifecycle spec named in docs/specs/README.md for `index`.
title: index: read-only segmentation preview for one file
